recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. No follow-up is needed for FHIR-23019 unless the work group later changes the three-state boolean guidance or requests a stronger conformance rule.
issue_request: FHIR-23019 was Published with a Persuasive with Modification resolution asking FHIR-core Questionnaire to clarify that boolean false should not be recorded unless selected and that enableWhen logic must distinguish false from no answer when relevant.
initial_application: Commit aaa68f89ca530b7c34b8a6a2ff6d4da8d20bc778, recorded in the Jira comment, added the Questionnaire 'Handling Boolean Answers' section. Later wording commits 0cb570cabec and 687e88f506 refined phrasing and checkbox examples without changing the core rule.
additional_context: Questionnaire is active in source/fhir.ini. The current source/questionnaire/questionnaire-notes.xml text says boolean questions have three possible states, explains when two-state controls are or are not sufficient, suggests tri-state/radio alternatives, and tells designers to account for non-answered boolean questions in enableWhen logic. A later Zulip questionnaire thread citing FHIR-23019 supports the same interpretation and no direct Confluence reference or conflicting community decision was found.
reconciliation: No source change was made because the active Questionnaire narrative already conveys both requested clarifications and further duplicated text would not change implementer understanding.

related_jiras.note: Later clarified checkbox and radio-button itemControl use for boolean items and made a small wording refinement in the same boolean section.
